name: Barrow of the old north
description: A turf mound over the dead of the country before the roads, kerbed in stone nobody living set. The high fells are sown with them, and the fell folk's oldest law is short: dig no barrow. Where the law has been kept the mound only watches you pass. Where it has not, the door stands levered open and the household walks its own grave-field, day and night, because whatever kept their hours in the dark went out the door with the robbers.

signs.title: OLD STONE
lines: the letters are worn past reading
somebody still keeps the moss off
